description: Metric gate expectations for the CI fixture fleet (tests/metric_gate_fleet.py). Floors/ceilings are promises; baselines pin the measured number so an unexplained move fails CI until scripts/update_metric_baselines.py records the reason. Measured on the platform's own stress-profile cells through the unmodified run_lco() harness.

soh_r2.note: Leave-cell-out SOH R^2 on the five gate-fleet cells. Floor is 4+ points below the measured value: tight enough that any real model/feature regression trips it, loose enough to absorb library-version float jitter.

rul_r2.note: Observed-EOL RUL R^2 on synthetic cells (coverage 0.68, extrapolated labels mixed in pre-v12 style). Floor 0.0: the model must at least not invert RUL ordering. Wide 50% tolerance because this metric is genuinely noisier across library versions on a 5-cell fleet.

baseline_soh_r2.note: The trivial cycle_number -> SOH line under the SAME five folds (batlab.validation.trivial_baseline.baseline_lco_r2) - the denominator of every '+X over the trivial baseline' claim on this fleet. Tracked since 2026-09-20, when a blank target row was found to delete it: sklearn's LinearRegression raises on a NaN in y, app/_data.py's bare `except` recorded None, and the claim lost its floor with no trace of why. NEGATIVE by design here - the five cells fade at very different rates (Cell5's own line reaches R^2 = -9.2 against the global fit), so one straight line is worse than predicting the mean, and that is the honest floor the model beats (soh_r2 baseline 0.9959). A CEILING rather than a floor because the risk is this number getting BETTER, which would quietly shrink the model's claimed advantage; its only inputs are cycle_number and soh_pct, so it is insensitive to feature and model changes by construction and a recorded move means the TARGET changed. Value verified bit-identical to the pre-fix implementation, and bit-identical under the 2026-09-20 environment (numpy 2.4.6 / pandas 3.0.3 / scikit-learn 1.9.0 / pybamm 26.6.2.0), i.e. the NaN tolerance changed no measured number on this fleet.
